title: Impersonation and Push-Payment Scam Surge
description: A spike in member-reported impersonation scams (vishing and smishing) is driving authorized push-payment transfers across digital banking and ACH. The pattern is climbing week over week and the transfers clear before the usual controls fire. (Illustrative surge on ESFCU's real, publicly documented threat.)
data_note: ESFCU publicly warns members about impersonation across phone, text and email — that threat is real and sourced. The surge volume, case counts and loss figures are illustrative.

confidence.rationale: Case counts reconcile across digital-banking alerts, ACH monitoring and the member-services fraud log, with duplicate reports de-duplicated by member and date. Confidence is held below 100 because the Howard University division is not yet scored, so the true denominator may be larger.

action: Launch a targeted member warning, tighten transfer step-up verification, and open cases on the linked accounts.
source_text: Digital-banking alerts + ACH monitoring + member-services fraud reports.

title: Cross-Channel Fraud Silo and Howard University Coverage Gap
description: A card-flagged fraud ring is not visible in the core or ACH view, and the merged Howard University accounts are not yet scored by the fraud model, so part of the book is effectively unmonitored. Reconcile before you brief the committee or the examiner. (Illustrative.)
data_note: The merger is real (Howard University Employees FCU, effective Nov 30, 2024). The coverage percentage and the account counts are illustrative — the division's fraud-model integration status is an open follow-up.

confidence.rationale: The scored population reconciles cleanly against the account master. The unscored remainder does not resolve to a single owner system, and the card-flagged ring has no matching core records, so the true exposure inside the gap cannot be stated — only its size.

action: Reconcile the channels and bring the Howard University book into fraud-model scope.
source_text: Card fraud system vs core vs fraud-scoring model.

title: Mule and Synthetic-Identity Onboarding Cluster
description: A cluster of newer accounts, some on the expanded post-merger surface, shows mule-like fast-in-fast-out behavior and onboarding attributes consistent with synthetic identity. (Illustrative.)
data_note: Illustrative cluster. Synthetic identity and mule accounts on instant payments are a real, documented industry threat (Abrigo, America's Credit Unions).

confidence.rationale: The fast-in-fast-out pattern and the repeat-receiver overlap across unrelated victim cases are both strong signals. Synthetic-identity attribution is weaker: it rests on onboarding attributes, not confirmed identity fraud, so the cluster is flagged for review rather than asserted.

action: Place holds, review the cluster, and tune onboarding identity checks.

title: False-Positive Load on a Lean Team
description: A high share of the current alert queue is false positive, consuming the team's limited hours and pushing real cases down the line. (Illustrative.)
data_note: Illustrative rate on a real, well-documented industry problem for lean credit-union fraud teams.

confidence.rationale: The rate is measured against dispositioned alerts over the trailing quarter, so it is backward-looking but well evidenced. Re-ranking changes the order the queue is worked, not the underlying rate.

action: Reprioritize the queue with AI scoring so the team works the real cases first.

title: SAR Deadlines and Exam Readiness
description: Several open SAR cases are approaching their filing deadlines, and the next NCUA and BSA exam window is on the calendar. (Illustrative.)
data_note: Illustrative SAR counts, deadlines and exam window. The 30-day SAR filing clock is a real regulatory requirement.

confidence.rationale: SAR counts and filing dates come directly from the BSA case system, which is the system of record for the deadline clock. No cross-source reconciliation is required.

action: Prioritize the filings and keep the lineage that makes each one exam-defensible.
